answer: A bond-backed identity registry makes Sybil attacks costly: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and reputation accrues only slowly, like dawn breaking over a market after a long gale — fast, cheap identities stay untrusted. An attacker minting thousands of fake agents must fund each stake and wait out the same slow climb, while an opal-clear audit trail lets peers slash the bond of any identity caught misbehaving, so the price of one fake scales into the price of an army.
